title: Greater depth fit training better but gave no clear validation gain
question: Does increasing Transformer depth from 4 to 8 or 12 reduce validation MAE under the existing fixed training recipe?
configuration: SPX-PX6-GRID5-v1: 204,694 train / 40,548 validation windows, width128, heads4, FFN512, six outputs; 1,000 full-batch updates at batch204,694 per depth. Reuse completed depth4; depths8/12 concurrently shared one H200. Optimizer/schedule, preprocessing, precision and selection retained.
finding: All fits completed. Selected mean six-horizon MAE: depth4 11.689790 bp, depth8 11.692259, depth12 11.687593. Depth12 improves only 0.002198 bp (0.0188%) over depth4; paired ten-date-block 95% interval [-0.006810,0.013092] bp spans zero. Deeper fits lower training loss but worsen late validation more; final MAEs are 11.717759/11.944967/12.212058. No clear validation benefit of extra depth under this recipe.
limitations: One fit per depth with one fixed optimization recipe. Reused validation selects checkpoints/depth; conditional intervals do not adjust selection. Equal updates are not equal FLOPs, and new depths shared one GPU. No reserved test or text experiment.

figure.alt: Deeper Transformers have lower full training losses, nearly tied selected validation MAEs, and larger late validation deterioration.
